title: Braciole
subtitle: Italian stuffed beef rolls braised in tomato
excerpt: Thin beef slices are filled with Parmesan, herbs and prosciutto, then rolled up and braised slowly in red wine and tomato. The result is tender, richly flavoured meat in a sauce so good you want to mop it up with bread. This is southern Italian Sunday cooking.
sourceNotes: Braciole is particularly associated with Neapolitan and Sicilian cooking. It is often made for Sunday lunch and slow-braised in a large pot of tomato sauce alongside other meats.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the sauce for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead. Braciole taste even better reheated the next day.

content.text: Bash the beef very thin before filling. A thick slice will not roll properly and will take much longer to braise. Secure each roll firmly with kitchen string so it does not unravel.

items.prepNote: sliced very thin (ask the butcher for beef braciole or schnitzel-cut slices)

content.text: Lay the beef slices flat. Cover each with a slice of prosciutto. Scatter over a pinch of Parmesan, chopped garlic and parsley. Season. Roll up firmly and tie with kitchen string.
Heat the oil in a wide heavy pan over high heat. Brown the rolls on all sides for about 5 minutes total. They should be well-coloured. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits. Let it bubble for 3 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes, stock and bay leaves. Season. Return the rolls to the pan. The sauce should come halfway up the rolls.
Cover and simmer very gently for 1 hour to 1.5 hours until the beef is completely tender. Turn the rolls once halfway through.
Remove the rolls. Snip off the string. If the sauce is thin, reduce it on high heat for 5 minutes. Return the rolls to the sauce. Serve with the sauce spooned over.

items.cause: Not tied tightly enough, or string came loose in the sauce
items.fix: Tie firmly with two pieces of string per roll. Check them at the halfway turn and retie if needed.

items.cause: Too much Parmesan and not enough fat in the filling
items.fix: Add a small slice of prosciutto fat to the filling next time, or a little olive oil mixed into the cheese and herbs.

content.text: Braciole is the great Sunday dish of Naples and Palermo. It is cooked alongside meatballs and sausages in the Sunday ragu. The sauce is used to dress pasta as a first course. The meat follows as the main.
